points.title: 童年与基础教育
points.description: 卢瑟福出生于新西兰纳尔逊附近的布赖特沃特，是家中12个孩子中的第四个。他的父亲詹姆斯是一位农民兼轮匠，母亲玛莎是一名教师。尽管家庭经济条件有限，但卢瑟福从小就展现出对科学和机械的浓厚兴趣。他在当地学校接受基础教育，表现出色，尤其是数学和科学方面。这段经历培养了他动手解决问题的能力，为他后来的科学探索奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: Rutherford was born in Brightwater, near Nelson, New Zealand, the fourth of twelve children to James Rutherford, a farmer and wheelwright, and Martha Thompson, a teacher. Despite limited family means, Rutherford showed early interest in science and mechanics. He received his basic education at local schools, excelling particularly in mathematics and science. This period developed his hands-on problem-solving abilities that would later characterize his scientific approach.

points.title: 大学教育与早期研究
points.description: 卢瑟福进入新西兰大学（现为坎特伯雷大学）学习，1893年获得文学学士和数学硕士学位，1894年获得物理学士学位。在大学期间，他发明了一种检测无线电波的方法，比马可尼更早，但未能获得专利。这段时期的研究经历使卢瑟福掌握了实验物理的基本技能，并激发了他对电磁现象的浓厚兴趣。他的导师亚历山大·麦克杜格尔对他影响深远，鼓励他继续深造。
points.descriptionEn: Rutherford attended the University of New Zealand (now University of Canterbury), earning a BA and MA in mathematics in 1893 and a BSc in 1894. During his university years, he invented a method for detecting radio waves, predating Marconi but failing to patent it. This period equipped him with fundamental experimental physics skills and sparked his interest in electromagnetic phenomena. His mentor Alexander Bickerton encouraged him to pursue further studies abroad.

points.title: 卡文迪许实验室研究
points.description: 卢瑟福获得奖学金前往英国剑桥大学的卡文迪许实验室，在J.J.汤姆逊指导下研究X射线和无线电。在这里，他发现了铀辐射的两种不同成分，并将其命名为α射线和β射线。这一发现奠定了他后来研究原子结构的基础。卢瑟福在剑桥期间还发明了电磁波检测器，并改进了无线电通讯技术。这段经历使卢瑟福进入了国际科学界的视野，并建立了与欧洲科学家的联系。
points.descriptionEn: Rutherford moved to the Cavendish Laboratory at Cambridge University on a scholarship, where he worked under J.J. Thomson studying X-rays and radioactivity. Here, he discovered that uranium radiation consisted of two different components, naming them alpha and beta rays. This discovery laid the foundation for his later work on atomic structure. Rutherford also invented an electromagnetic wave detector and improved radio communication technology during this period, establishing connections with European scientists and gaining recognition in the international scientific community.

points.title: 麦吉尔大学突破
points.description: 卢瑟福接受麦吉尔大学的物理学教授职位，在这里他取得了最重要的科学成就之一。1902年，他与弗雷德里克·索迪共同提出放射性衰变理论，推翻了原子不可变的传统观念。1908年，他因研究放射性元素获得诺贝尔化学奖。在麦吉尔期间，卢瑟福还发现了氡气，并精确测量了α粒子的性质。这些研究成果彻底改变了人们对原子结构的理解，为现代物理学奠定了基础。卢瑟福在蒙特利尔的时期是他科学创造力最为旺盛的阶段之一。
points.descriptionEn: Rutherford accepted a professorship in physics at McGill University, where he achieved some of his most significant scientific breakthroughs. In 1902, he co-authored the radioactive decay theory with Frederick Soddy, challenging the traditional view of atomic permanence. In 1908, he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for his work on radioactive elements. During his time in Montreal, Rutherford also discovered radon and accurately measured the properties of alpha particles. These findings revolutionized understanding of atomic structure and laid the foundation for modern physics. His Montreal period represented one of his most scientifically productive phases.

points.title: 原子结构革命
points.description: 卢瑟福回到英国，担任曼彻斯特大学物理系主任。1911年，他通过α粒子散射实验提出了原子核模型，认为原子中心有一个带正电的核，电子围绕核旋转。这一革命性理论彻底改变了人们对原子结构的理解。1919年，他首次实现人工核反应，将氮原子转变为氧原子。1925-1930年，他担任英国皇家学会主席。在曼彻斯特期间，卢瑟福培养了多位诺贝尔奖得主，包括尼尔斯·玻尔和查尔斯·威尔逊。他的实验室成为世界物理学研究中心，被称为'现代原子物理学的摇篮'。
points.descriptionEn: Rutherford returned to Britain as Chair of Physics at the University of Manchester. In 1911, he proposed the nuclear model of the atom based on alpha particle scattering experiments, suggesting a positively charged nucleus with electrons orbiting around it. This revolutionary theory fundamentally changed understanding of atomic structure. In 1919, he achieved the first artificial nuclear transmutation, converting nitrogen into oxygen. From 1925-1930, he served as President of the Royal Society. During his Manchester years, Rutherford mentored numerous Nobel laureates including Niels Bohr and Charles Wilson. His laboratory became a world center for physics research, earning the title 'cradle of modern atomic physics.'

supporter.zh: 卢瑟福被誉为'原子物理学之父'，他的开创性研究彻底改变了人类对物质本质的理解。他提出的原子核模型为现代物理学奠定了基础，他的放射性研究开创了核物理学新领域。作为一位杰出的实验科学家，卢瑟福不仅取得了重大科学突破，还培养了一代顶尖物理学家，建立了世界级的科研传统。他的科学精神和创新思维激励着后来的研究者，对20世纪科学发展产生了深远影响。
supporter.en: Rutherford is hailed as the 'father of nuclear physics' for his groundbreaking research that fundamentally transformed humanity's understanding of matter. His nuclear model of the atom laid the foundation for modern physics, while his work on radioactivity pioneered the field of nuclear physics. As an exceptional experimental scientist, Rutherford not only achieved major scientific breakthroughs but also mentored a generation of leading physicists and established world-class research traditions. His scientific spirit and innovative thinking continue to inspire researchers, leaving a profound impact on 20th-century science.

critic.zh: 批评者指出卢瑟福的理论存在局限性，例如他的原子模型无法解释电子的稳定性和光谱现象，这后来由玻尔等人完善。此外，卢瑟福对某些科学观点过于固执，如长期不相信量子力学的完备性。作为诺贝尔化学奖得主而非物理学奖得主，也反映了他研究领域的局限性。他的管理风格有时被描述为专断，与学生关系紧张。这些批评提醒我们即使是伟大的科学家也有其历史局限性和个人缺陷。
critic.en: Critics point out limitations in Rutherford's theories, such as his atomic model's inability to explain electron stability and spectral phenomena, which were later addressed by Bohr and others. Additionally, Rutherford was sometimes overly rigid in his scientific views, such as his long-standing disbelief in the completeness of quantum mechanics. His Nobel Prize in Chemistry rather than Physics also reflects limitations in his research scope. His management style has been described as autocratic, with strained relationships with some students. These criticisms remind us that even great scientists have historical limitations and personal flaws.

objective.zh: 在历史学界，卢瑟福被视为从经典物理学向现代物理学过渡的关键人物。他的研究既体现了19世纪实验物理学的严谨方法，又开创了20世纪量子物理学的新方向。流行文化中，卢瑟福常被描绘为'原子拆解者'，象征着人类对微观世界的探索精神。他的实验室成为现代物理学研究的典范，培养了多位诺贝尔奖得主。卢瑟福的遗产不仅在于科学发现，更在于他建立的研究传统和科学方法，影响了整个20世纪的科学发展轨迹。
objective.en: In historical scholarship, Rutherford is viewed as a pivotal figure in the transition from classical to modern physics. His work embodied the rigorous methods of 19th-century experimental physics while pioneering new directions in 20th-century quantum physics. In popular culture, Rutherford is often portrayed as the 'atom smasher,' symbolizing humanity's exploration of the microscopic world. His laboratory became a model for modern physics research, producing multiple Nobel laureates. Rutherford's legacy extends beyond his scientific discoveries to include the research traditions and methodologies he established, influencing the trajectory of 20th-century scientific development.

self.zh: 科学就是关于事物的组织，而不是关于事物的收集。
self.en: Science is the organization of knowledge, so that it may be used.

others.zh: 卢瑟福是一位具有非凡直觉的物理学家，他能够从最复杂的实验数据中提炼出最简单的真理。
others.en: Rutherford was a physicist of extraordinary intuition who could distill the simplest truths from the most complex experimental data.
